  (back-compat: a no-op if no loop is injected). `earning_pipeline.py` injects the `LearningLoop`.































































































































































































































































- Cold-start safe: aggregates with `sample_size < MIN_SAMPLES` return a NEUTRAL prior + low































































































































































































































































  confidence; never a hard reject from insufficient data.































































































































































































































































## Reusable Skill/Task Capability Framework (v2.0.36e)































































































































































































































































Coding is ONE capability among many. A reusable framework lets the system reason about ANY job































































































































type without spawning a heavyweight agent per type.































































































































































































































































- `agents/capability_registry.py` — `CapabilityCategory` (seed taxonomy: READING, WRITING, EDITING,































































































































  RESEARCH, DATA, TRANSCRIPTION, CODING, TESTING, QA, DOCUMENTS, CONTENT, WEB_RESEARCH, AUTOMATION,































































































































  ANALYSIS, ADMINISTRATIVE, CRYPTO, OTHER) + `CapabilityRegistry`, seeded with the system's ACTUAL































































































































  capabilities (each mapped to a real tool and, where one exists, an existing `skills/*.md` file --































































































































  reuse, not duplication). The taxonomy is open: new capabilities register at runtime.































































































































- `agents/task_spec.py` — `Task` dataclass carries task_type, required_capabilities, inputs,































































































































  expected_outputs, tools_required, estimated_effort, validation_method, human_required,































































































































  execution_mode, payment_conditions. `infer_task_requirements()` is a deterministic, offline































































































































  lexicon that maps natural language -> required capabilities; an LLM may be plugged in via































































































































  `set_requirement_inferrer()` but it FAILS SAFE and is never authoritative. `build_task()` and































































































































  `task_from_opportunity()` (which reuses the `Opportunity` model) build Tasks.































































































































- `agents/task_validator.py` — `CapabilityValidator` is the DETERMINISTIC, authoritative gate































































































































  (per the security principle: the LLM is NOT the source of truth). For each required capability:































































































































    - system + automatable           -> served automatically































































































































    - system + human-only            -> served via a human (if `human_available`)































































































































    - not in system + human-capable  -> requires a human































































































































    - not in system + not human      -> HARD UNSUPPORTED































































































































  Verdict: fully_automatable / partially_automatable / human_required / unsupported.































































































































  **Unsupported tasks are NEVER reported executable** (`is_executable=False`); the validator writes































































































































  the authoritative `execution_mode` / `human_required` back onto the `Task`.































































































































































































































































Example verdicts (deterministic, offline):































































































































- "Proofread 20 pages"      -> fully_automatable (READING + EDITING + DOCUMENT_QA)































































































































- "Fix Python bug"          -> fully_automatable (CODING + DEBUGGING + TESTING)































































































































- "Research 30 companies"   -> fully_automatable (WEB_RESEARCH + DATA + ANALYSIS)































































































































- "Transcribe audio"        -> human_required (TRANSCRIPTION has no in-system tool; a human can do it)































































































































- "Transcribe audio" with `human_available=False` -> unsupported (cannot be performed)































































































































































































































































No per-capability execution agents were created (explicitly out of scope); the framework is the































































































































shared capability-matching layer that any future executor can consult.































































































































## Dynamic Opportunity Discovery Scheduler (v2.0.36f)































































































































MrBot1000 runs a STEADY, SELF-DRIVING discovery stream — the user never has to ask "find me jobs".































































A history-aware scheduler decides WHAT to search, WHEN, HOW OFTEN, which categories to prioritize,































































which searches to reduce, which sources to suspend, and which new sources to explore.































































































































- `agents/discovery_strategies.py` — `SearchStrategyGenerator` builds search strategies from MANY































































  origins (not one static query): SKILL, HISTORICAL_CATEGORY, USER_PREFERENCE, EMERGING,































































  PAST_SUCCESS_TERM, PLATFORM_TERM, EXPLORATION, plus an OPTIONAL LLM suggester that FAILS SAFE.































































  Failed search terms are excluded. The LLM only SUGGESTS; it is never given an external action —































































  every output is a validated `SearchStrategy` object fed to a provider interface.































































- `agents/discovery_scheduler.py` — `DiscoveryScheduler` + `tick()`. Respects (deterministic):































































  platform rate limits (platform_throttle), source cooldowns, resource constraints































































  (max_tasks/concurrency), model availability, configured working hours, opportunity freshness,































































  duplicate detection (DiscoveryEngine), source reliability (memory), and error backoff.































































  History-driven decisions:































































    * reliable + profitable source  -> shorter interval, higher priority (exploit more).































































    * low-yield / high-listing source -> longer interval, reduced priority (may suspend).































































    * recently-profitable category   -> boosted exploration weight.































































    * error streak                   -> exponential suspension that RECOVERS (one bad result































































      never permanently kills a source).































































  Exploration/exploitation balance: an exploration floor guarantees known winners are NOT fully































































  exploited; new sources/categories/strategies keep getting a chance.































































- `earning_memory.search_strategy` (NEW table) — the learning link: each generated strategy is































































  recorded (`record_search_strategy`) and its outcomes learned (`record_strategy_outcome`,































































  `top_search_strategies`). Discovered opportunities are tagged with `strategy:<id>` provenance so































































  the system learns which search strategies actually produce profitable work.































































- `earning_pipeline.run_discovery_cycle()` — injects `DiscoveryScheduler` and runs a tick through a































































  VALIDATED `discover_fn` (built-in sources only). The LLM is never invoked for network calls here.































































































































Security: discovery executes ONLY through validated provider interfaces; the LLM may suggest strategy































































ideas but cannot perform uncontrolled external actions.































































## Search Strategy Memory (v2.0.36g)































































MrBot1000 learns not only which PLATFORMS work, but which SEARCH STRATEGIES work — and optimizes































for useful, legitimate, PROFITABLE opportunities, not raw result volume.































































- `earning_memory.search_strategy` — extended with the full economic schema: `query`,































  `normalized_query` (stopword-stripped canonical form; `_normalize_query` groups semantically































  related searches), `platform`, `category`, `task_type`, `source`, `result_count`,































  `useful_result_count`, `duplicate_count`, `accepted`, `completed`, `paid`, `net_revenue`,































  `effort_sum`. `record_strategy_result()` learns economic outcomes; `reward_sum` is a composite































  usefulness reward (useful + completed + paid + net_revenue, minus duplicates).































- `_strategy_usefulness()` returns a COLD-START-NEUTRAL prior (`MIN_SAMPLES`) for novel strategies,































  so historical performance NEVER permanently suppresses a fresh search. `top_search_strategies































  (by='usefulness')` ranks exploitation on the composite metric (NOT result count);































  `explore_search_strategies()` surfaces novel/under-tried searches so exploration stays alive.































  `get_successful_search_terms` / `get_failed_search_terms` are usefulness- and cold-start-aware































  (a query is "failed" only with enough samples AND zero useful results).































- Provenance -> outcome loop: discovery tags each opportunity with `strategy:<id>` provenance;































  when an opportunity reaches a final outcome, `opportunity_lifecycle.mark_final_outcome` fires an































  optional `outcome_callback` (deterministic, fails-safe) that the pipeline wires to































  `_record_strategy_outcome` — it extracts `strategy:<id>` from the provenance and records the































  ECONOMIC outcome into Search Strategy Memory. The discovery scheduler then ranks exploitation by































  usefulness and keeps novel searches explorable.































































Security: recording is deterministic (no LLM, no network); the LLM never performs an external































action during discovery or outcome learning.































## Opportunity Portfolio & Work Queue (v2.0.36h)































MrBot1000 can discover many opportunities simultaneously but only act on a sensible subset — prioritized by a configurable policy and bounded by hard overcommit limits.































- `agents/opportunity_portfolio.py` — `WorkStatus` enum (16 states: NEW, EVALUATING, QUALIFIED, RECOMMENDED, AWAITING_APPROVAL, READY, IN_PROGRESS, BLOCKED, WAITING_EXTERNAL, COMPLETED, PAYMENT_PENDING, PAID, FAILED, REJECTED, EXPIRED, ABANDONED) with a `WorkStatusConfig` mapping each to a lifecycle stage. `PortfolioEntry` carries the portfolio-level fields the user asked for: priority, expected_value, expected_hourly_value, deadline, confidence, risk, effort, next_action, waiting_reason, evidence_status, payment_status, skill_fit, policy_score. `OpportunityPortfolio` is sqlite-backed for persistence and recovery after restart. `transition_work_status` validates against `VALID_WORK_TRANSITIONS` then delegates lifecycle-affecting moves to the lifecycle tracker — it WALKS the lifecycle's transition graph (BFS over `_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS`) so intermediate stages (e.g., queued→applied→in_progress) are applied and the lifecycle stays authoritative at every step.















- `QueuePolicy` — configurable weights (expected_hourly, confidence, risk, skill_fit, deadline_urgency, effort, priority_override) with a **pluggable scorer callable** so the formula is NOT hardcoded. Optimizes for useful, profitable, low-risk, good-skill-fit, urgent work — NOT raw result count.















- `CapacityConfig` — configurable overcommit limits (active tasks, pending applications, simultaneous, high-risk, financial exposure, per-platform). `WorkQueue.select_next` walks the prioritized list and skips any entry that would exceed a limit — only as many as capacity allows are selected, even if 50 are queued.















- `resolve_next_action` + `apply_next` — deterministic next-action per status and a chain-advance helper (NEW→...→PAID).















- `earning_pipeline.py` — `EarningPipeline` gains an optional `portfolio=` kwarg (back-compat: works with None); `evaluate()` syncs EV, confidence, skill_fit, risk, effort from the intelligence verdict to the portfolio. End-to-end: discovery → evaluate → portfolio sync → queue selection with overcommit gates.































Security: deterministic sync only; the LLM never performs an external action during portfolio recording.















## Generalized Task Execution Framework (v2.0.36i)















MrBot1000 expands from "coding worker" toward generalized task execution with a 14-step pipeline, task-specific deterministic validators, and human-in-the-loop gates.















- `agents/task_validators.py` — deterministic validators per the user's spec. `CodingValidator` (syntax/tests/diff), `WritingValidator` (length/requirements coverage/formatting), `ResearchValidator` (source count/citations/quality), `DataValidator` (schema/row counts/duplicates), `TranscriptionValidator` (format/timestamp integrity/completeness), `DocumentValidator` (required fields/formatting/coverage). `ValidationReport` records each check. `VALIDATOR_REGISTRY` maps task types → validators; `get_validator()` falls back to WritingValidator.







- `agents/human_gates.py` — `HumanGateManager` determines when human input is REQUIRED (never bypasses). Eight gate categories: identity verification, sensitive information, contracts, payments, signatures, captchas, irreversible actions, platform-specific manual interaction. `clear_gate` records human clearance; `get_pending_gates` lists uncleared gates.







- `agents/task_executor.py` — `TaskExecutor` drives the 14-step pipeline: inspect requirements → identify capabilities/tools → determine feasibility → create plan → identify human actions → execute → validate → prepare deliverables → submit → wait → verify → record evidence → learn. `ExecutionContext` tracks state; `ExecutionPlan`/`ExecutionResult` dataclasses. Pipeline stops at human gates (AWAITING_APPROVAL), fails on validation failure.







- `earning_pipeline.py` — `EarningPipeline` creates a `TaskExecutor` wired to the portfolio, capability validator, and human gate manager.















Security: deterministic validators only — the LLM never decides completion. Human gates are hard stops that cannot be bypassed.







## Unified Economic Accounting Layer (v2.0.36j)







A single, honest accounting layer for all opportunity types. Distinguishes advertised value, expected value, realized gross revenue, realized expenses, realized net profit, verified revenue, and unverified revenue.







- `agents/economic_accounting.py` — `ExpenseCategory` enum (PLATFORM_FEE, TRANSACTION_FEE, GAS, LLM_COST, API_COST, TOOL_COST, OTHER). `EconomicProfile` dataclass (advertised/expected/realized/verified/unverified/pending revenue, expenses by category, realized_net, roi, net_hourly_rate, prediction accuracy). `EconomicAccounting` class (pure compute over EvidenceStore; revenue only from VERIFIED payment evidence; USD + crypto conversion; aggregate portfolio metrics).



- `earning_pipeline.py` — `EarningPipeline` creates an `EconomicAccounting` wired to the EvidenceStore. The pipeline report uses the accounting layer for verified/unverified revenue, expenses, net profit, ROI, net hourly rate, and expenses by category.







Security: Revenue is realized ONLY when appropriate VERIFIED payment evidence exists. Advertised payment, successful submission, and generated deliverables are NOT revenue.



## Self-Audit & Continuous-Improvement Layer (v2.0.36j)



A self-audit engine that identifies improvement opportunities without modifying safety constraints.



- `agents/self_audit.py` — `AuditCategory` enum (14 categories: repeated_failures, prediction_errors, bad_strategies, poor_platforms, poor_categories, poor_task_types, low_performing_variants, high_cost_workflows, human_intervention, execution_failures, stale_providers, stale_categories, security_problems, documentation_drift). `Severity` enum. `AuditFinding` dataclass (observation/evidence/confidence/recommended_change/expected_benefit/expected_risk/affected_components/test_requirements). `AuditReport`. `SelfAuditEngine` (analyzes memory+evidence_store+accounting; produces structured findings; no mutations to security policy).

- `earning_pipeline.py` — `EarningPipeline` creates a `SelfAuditEngine` wired to memory, evidence_store, and accounting.

================================================================================
ACTUAL COMMUNICATION ARCHITECTURE (v2.0.36k-comms) — verified by tests
================================================================================
Implemented 2026-08-14. Supersedes the stale "SharedContext JSON mirror" notes
elsewhere in this file. Code is authoritative; this section reflects what runs.

COORDINATOR / CoordinatorWorker: DOES NOT EXIST. All "CoordinatorWorker" /
SharedContext cross-model signal/decision APIs (query_model, share_decision,
add_signal, get_signals, complete_task, get_pending_tasks) are DEAD CODE and
were never called at runtime.

PROTOCOL (agents/comms.py):
- Message: message_id, correlation_id (=message_id if unset), source, destination,
  message_type, timestamp, priority, payload(dict), status, parent_message_id.
  Envelope types: USER_REQUEST, TASK_REQUEST, TASK_RESULT, MODEL_REQUEST,
  MODEL_RESULT, STATE_UPDATE, OPPORTUNITY_UPDATE, EVIDENCE_UPDATE, MEMORY_QUERY,
  MEMORY_RESULT, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, APPROVAL_RESULT, ERROR, NOTIFICATION.
- EventBus: pure-Python, thread-safe pub/sub (no Qt dependency). Single instance.
  Route by type/source/destination. Enforces:
    * NO self-loop (destination == source rejected).
    * NO ping-pong: a REQUEST routed back to a node that already initiated in the
      same correlation_id chain is rejected (prior-source walk + edge replay detect).
    * NO duplicate execution: same request message_id delivered once (dedup).
    * Cancellation via CancellationToken; errors published as ERROR(correlation_id).
    * Persistence: MessageLog (agents/comms_log.py, sqlite) records every message;
      mark_orphans_cancelled() flips PENDING/IN_FLIGHT -> CANCELLED on restart.
- QtEventBridge: optional QObject that subscribes to the bus and re-emits a Qt
  Signal so GUI widgets observe events on the GUI thread (no model internals).

RUNTIME FLOW (verified by tests/test_comms.py + tests/test_comms_integration.py):
  GUI._human_send ──publish USER_REQUEST(gui->chat)──▶ EventBus
    └▶ SummarizerThread._on_bus_message ─enqueue─▶ _handle_chat
         ├─ chat intent: Chat model answers → publish MODEL_RESULT(chat->gui)
         └─ task intent: publish TASK_REQUEST(chat->manager, correlation preserved)
                              └▶ ManagerThread._on_bus_message ─enqueue msg_queue─▶
                                  _handle_bus_message → CEO flow →
                                  publish TASK_RESULT/MODEL_RESULT(manager->chat) +
                                  chat_reply Signal (back-compat GUI display)
  earning_pipeline.track_opportunity ──publish OPPORTUNITY_UPDATE──▶ EventBus
    └▶ GUI QtEventBridge._on_bus_event → dashboard log line
  chat_router.build_runtime_context: prefers LIVE lifecycle/evidence/memory
    providers when supplied; falls back to the legacy SharedContext JSON file
    only when no live provider is given. The JSON mirror is now READ-ONLY and is
    the deprecated path.

THREADING: unchanged — GUI thread, ManagerThread (main model), SummarizerThread
(chat model) remain separate. Queues (human_queue/task_queue/msg_queue on Manager;
_chat_queue on Summarizer) carry structured Messages; the bus is the routing +
observability layer. GUI is never blocked by model calls (proven by
test_chat_responsive in tests/test_comms.py).

EVIDENCE OF CORRECTNESS (19 protocol + integration tests, all green):
  responsiveness, task-reach, result-reach, gui-updates, correlation-fanout,
  error-propagation, cancellation, no-dup-exec, no-circular-loop, restart-safety,
  GUI↔Chat↔Manager structured routing with correlation, Qt bridge delivery.
